The RP corner's third page on the force in three days (Gur 10-28, Doran 10-29, MacLean 10-30), the first whose visible text reaches the Strait and the deal's terms. object.label: the next offensive against Iran — the force (slate01; PG01 §5): read from the RP corner's strategist as a menu — five options after the vote, from a deal to escalation, with the visible page covering the two least escalatory. The strike's clock is the vote's, and the reason is stated: 'a significant military escalation today would spook the financial markets and harm Republican candidates next Tuesday' (¶1). The Strait is on the page as the deal's first issue and as the thing a quick deal would 'surrender'; H6's throughput claim appears hedged — escorts 'appear to have restored oil transits to near pre-war levels' (¶3)

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: how Trump can fight Iran after the midterms
lines.note: THE HEADLINE: 'how', not 'whether' — the strike pre-credited to the calendar
lines.zWhy: a headline that asks how presumes the fight follows the vote

lines.quote: win or lose, once the midterms are over the president will have more options than he does right now — none a sure path to victory
lines.note: the dek: the vote as a release of options, not a check on them
lines.zWhy: a vote that widens the menu is not one that closes it

lines.quote: five options after the midterms, more than he has now — a significant escalation today would spook the financial markets and harm Republican candidates next Tuesday
lines.note: THE MECHANISM STATED PLAINLY: the strike's clock is the vote's, for the market's and the ballot's sake — the gas↔votes predicate from the RP side, as a planning constraint
lines.zWhy: a strike held back only for Tuesday's sake is a strike held, not relented

lines.quote: recent news reports suggest the president is leaning in the direction of some form of renewed military action
lines.note: the object dated by report — the page's lowest line

lines.quote: make a deal — still a possibility; the key issues the status of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program; both sides' public positions irreconcilable at the moment
lines.note: →H6 and the terms: the Strait's status as the deal's first issue; 'irreconcilable' the one vehicle
lines.zWhy: a deal 'still a possibility' with positions irreconcilable is a strike not yet off the table

lines.quote: ISW's 'sequencing' problem — Iran: lift the naval blockade, provide sanctions relief, recognize Iranian control over the strait before any concessions
lines.note: Iran's terms, sourced — the toll's ledger from the other side (iran-terms: blockade, relief, control)
lines.zWhy: terms that start with recognizing Iran's control are the counter-claim to the holder's; the gap is the war

lines.quote: I, too, prefer my enemy's surrender as a precondition for further discussion
lines.note: the aside — irony as the vehicle; the page's highest line
lines.zWhy: a strategist mocking the terms does not expect the deal

lines.quote: Trump tested a conciliatory approach with the June memorandum — recognizing Iranian sovereignty in the strait as a precondition for nuclear talks; the deal collapsed in less than two weeks
lines.note: THE RECORD: a signed recognition of Iranian sovereignty in the strait, in June — the control claim's own history (H6's shadow against its record). As-of June
lines.zWhy: a deal that lasted two weeks is the precedent for the next one failing

lines.quote: for Trump to close a deal quickly he would effectively have to surrender the strait to Iran
lines.note: the deal priced in the strait; 'surrender' the vehicle
lines.zWhy: if the quick deal costs the strait, the author expects no quick deal — and the force stays

lines.quote: the blockade of Iranian ports is doing meaningful economic damage; escort operations in the Strait — essentially a counterblockade — appear to have restored oil transits to near pre-war levels; other commodities less clear
lines.note: H6 FROM RP: the throughput claim restated as 'appear to have restored … near pre-war levels' — CENTCOM's number without the number, hedged twice
lines.zWhy: transits 'near pre-war' read toward relief; 'appear' and 'less clear' pull back; a hold is not a stop

lines.quote: Trump could preserve this status quo and wait to see if economic pressure forces Iran's regime to surrender, or else risk collapse
lines.note: option two: the war as a hold; 'surrender', 'collapse' the vehicles
lines.zWhy: a status quo kept until surrender is the war continuing by other means
